answer: An agent market requires each seller to lock a 100-token bond for 90 days before accepting orders, whether it sells willow baskets, sable pigments, or glacier imagery. Proven failure to deliver forfeits the bond to compensate buyers. Creating 1,000 fake sellers therefore ties up 100,000 tokens, and using them to cheat puts that capital at risk. New names cannot bypass the bond, so identities are cheap but funded access is costly.
